findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Delete the entire Special Cases section or replace it with genuinely new information not already covered in Program Overview.
findings.violation: This text duplicates the Program Overview section (lines 5-6) verbatim, creating confusion about whether this is new information or a repeated section.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Break this into 3-4 shorter sentences. Example: "The policy allows one device per category. A second device requires manager approval. The benefits team must confirm the role genuinely requires fieldwork away from a fixed desk. The second device counts against the same annual category budget."
findings.violation: This sentence is a single unwieldy run-on of 59 words that makes the policy nearly impossible to parse. Multiple nested clauses cloud the core rule about second devices.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. The team logs each request the moment it arrives. The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department. Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Insert a sentence clarifying the approval chain, e.g., "The designated approver (usually the manager) has two business days to review and approve."
findings.violation: This process description has a logical gap: the section does not explain who actually approves the request (manager, finance, both) before the team schedules reimbursement.

findings.evidence: "A workspace used only occasionally for calls does not meet the bar the stipend policy sets."
findings.fix: Replace with specific criteria, e.g., "A workspace must be used for at least 50% of work hours to qualify. A workspace used only occasionally for calls does not meet this threshold."
findings.violation: This rule is circular and undefined - it refers to "the bar" without specifying what that bar is, making it impossible for an applicant to know if their workspace qualifies.

findings.evidence: "However, an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Add a clarification: "When a request is incomplete, the two-business-day clock pauses. An automatic reminder is sent after three days. The clock restarts once the missing item is submitted."
findings.violation: It is unclear what happens to the two-business-day timeline mentioned earlier (line 26) when a request is paused. Does the clock restart, or is there a separate three-day clock for incomplete requests?

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Define the term at first use: "A stipend item is a single piece of equipment eligible for reimbursement. You record each stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles every stipend item against the request log monthly. Payroll releases the reimbursement amount after that review."
findings.violation: The term "stipend item" is never defined, and the text shifts inconsistently between second person ("you") and passive voice, making roles unclear.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Delete this line or replace it with information specific to the Questions and Updates section, such as "Contact the people operations office for budget and catalog updates."
findings.violation: This sentence duplicates line 7 from the Program Overview section, suggesting either copy-paste error or misplaced content.

findings.evidence: "Also, the portal saves a draft automatically every few minutes."
findings.fix: Replace with a specific interval, e.g., "The portal saves a draft automatically every 30 seconds" or "saves a draft every time you pause typing for 10 seconds."
findings.violation: The frequency "every few minutes" is too vague and could lead to data loss if an employee loses their connection between saves.

findings.evidence: "Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Clarify what the employee sees: "Then, the employee reviews a summary showing the equipment cost, requested delivery date, and any workspace confirmations already on file. After reviewing, the employee submits the final request."
findings.violation: It is not clear what "confirmation summary" means or when a confirmation has been performed at this stage of the process, since the workspace confirmation review happens after submission (per line 15).
